postings.conferenceName: 3rd SOCAISA WORKSHOP
postings.conferenceText: Bridging SOC, AI & IoTSOCAISA explores the convergence of Service-Oriented Computing, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet of Things — addressing the critical challenges of interoperability and scalability in the design of intelligent, interconnected systems.Interoperability ChallengesIn the context of SOC and IoT, interoperability remains a fundamental challenge due to the diverse nature of devices, protocols, and service interfaces. AI techniques offer promising solutions by enabling systems to autonomously understand and adapt to varying data formats and communication protocols. Semantic technologies and NLP can standardize service descriptions, enhancing discovery and composition across heterogeneous environments.Scalability SolutionsAs IoT deployments expand exponentially, generating massive data volumes, SOC frameworks must efficiently process and manage them at scale. AI-driven approaches — edge computing, distributed learning, federated architectures — enable decentralized decision-making, reducing latency and enhancing scalability. Predictive analytics and dynamic resource allocation allow SOC architectures to adapt to real-time demand.AI as a Convergence EngineArtificial Intelligence is no longer a standalone layer: it acts as the convergence engine that makes SOC and IoT systems adaptive, context-aware, and self-healing. From LLMs as service orchestrators to federated learning across IoT nodes, AI fundamentally reshapes how services are discovered, composed, and governed.Research & PracticeSOCAISA brings together researchers and practitioners from three communities to produce cross-disciplinary insights, establish a shared vocabulary, and define a forward-looking research agenda. The workshop covers the full spectrum — from formal models and middleware design to real-world deployments and benchmarking frameworks.Research Focus AreasThe workshop welcomes contributions across the following themes, without being limited to them.AI & ServicesAI Integration in Service-Oriented Systems AI-Driven Service Orchestration and Composition AI-Enhanced Service Discovery and Recommendation AI-Based SLA Management AI-Driven Adaptive and Self-Healing Systems AI for Quality of Service (QoS) Optimization AI-Enabled Security and Privacy in SOC Intent-Based Service ComputingLLMs & Generative AILLMs as Service Orchestrators in IoT Environments Generative AI for Automated Service Configuration Small Language Models (SLMs) for Resource-Constrained IoT Explainable AI (XAI) for Trustworthy Service SystemsIoT & Edge ComputingAI for IoT and Edge Computing Integration Context-Aware AI Technologies for Services and IoT Edge-Cloud Continuum Architectures for Intelligent IoT Distributed LLM Inference at the Edge AI-Enabled Sustainable IoT SolutionsInteroperability & SemanticsSemantic-Based IoT Solutions for Interoperability Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving IoT ServicesData, Cloud & InfrastructureBig Data Management in Service-Oriented IoT Microservices and Serverless Architectures for Scalable IoT Carbon-Aware Service Scheduling in IoT InfrastructuresEmerging ParadigmsDigital Twin Frameworks for IoT Service Management Blockchain for Decentralized Trust and SLA Enforcement AI-Driven SOC for Smart Health, Smart Cities & Industry 4.0Submission & PublicationAuthors are invited to submit original, unpublished research contributions.Format RequirementsFull papers must not exceed 12 pages (including references and appendices), formatted according to the Springer LNCS template.Papers must be submitted as PDF files via the EasyChair platform. If you encounter any issue during submission, contact us at Karim.guennoun@ehtp.ac.ma.Each submission will be reviewed by at least three members of the international program committee, evaluated on originality, significance, technical soundness, and clarity.PublicationAll accepted papers will be published in the workshop proceedings as part of the Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) series by Springer.At least one author of each accepted paper must register and present at the workshop. Registration follows the terms of the main ICSOC 2026 conference.

postings.conferenceName: 2nd International Workshop on XR for Challenging Environments
postings.conferenceText: We invite submissions to the 2nd International Workshop on XR for Challenging Environments (XR4CE), a satellite event of EuroXR 2026 and VWA Forum 2026. Continuing the conversation on how XR can best support the fulfilment of mission-critical work, the event will be held in Valencia, Spain.Workshop Theme: From Co-existence to CollaborationChallenging environments such as emergency response, public safety, advanced manufacturing, or space missions demand high levels of human performance under stress. This workshop investigates how XR-based training, assistance and augmentation can support people working in high-stakes, uncertain, and demanding contexts. To successfully address this challenge, enabling and nurturing active collaboration among actors (practitioners, researchers, technologies, systems) is essential.To this end, we welcome 2-4 page position papers featuring novel concepts, empirical findings, provocative statements, or case studies addressing topics including:* The Augmented Professional: Cognitive load, skill evolution, and human agency in mission-critical XR use.* Human-AI Teaming: Moving beyond AI as a tool toward AI as a team member - shared situational awareness, role negotiation, and real-time coordination in high-stakes XR environments.* Multi-Agent Coordination: Design challenges for environments where humans, robots, and AI agents share the same operational and information space without stepping on each other.* Multi-Stakeholder Design: Co-designing XR for challenging environments with operators, managers, regulators, and end-users as active participants rather than informants.* XR as a Collaboration Medium: Using XR to support shared awareness and communication among distributed or co-located teams in challenging environments.* Cross-Domain Knowledge Transfer: What emergency medicine can learn from military XR, what industrial operations can borrow from healthcare - and how to make that transfer systematic.* Design for Operational Deployment: Building XR systems that hold up under field realities: degraded communications, physical stress, time pressure, and environmental uncertainty.* Transfer of Training: Which skills, habits, and mental models carry over from XR training to live deployment, and which break down under real operational conditions?* Researcher-Practitioner Partnership: Structures and formats that enable genuine two-way learning between academic researchers and field experts, beyond one-off consultation.* Cross-Disciplinary Research Integration: How HCI, AI, cognitive science, and domain practice can move from parallel work toward genuinely integrated XR4CE-related research agendas.* Case Studies: XR-in-use experiences and lessons learned from emergency response, industrial operations, healthcare, and other challenging environments.Important Dates:* Submission deadline: Sep 23, 2026 (AoE)* Notifications of acceptance: Oct 5, 2026* Workshop event: Nov 3, 2026 (morning)Submission Format:* 2–4 page position papers (see workshop website for details)Website: https://xr4ce-eur26.tech-experience.atOrganizers:* Raimund Schatz, AIT Austrian Institute of Technology* Helmut Schrom-Feiertag, AIT Austrian Institute of Technology* Lea Skorin-Kapov, University of Zagreb* Jan-Niklas Voigt-Antons, Hamm-Lippstadt University of Applied Sciences (HSHL)* Leif Oppermann, Fraunhofer FIT & Virtual Worlds Association

AI, with its ability to process vast amounts of data and learn from patterns, is enhancing decision-making, automating complex tasks, and driving efficiency. CPS, which integrates physical systems with digital computing, enables real-time monitoring, control, and optimization of processes in diverse applications.
